title: Ang 1105–1106: Namdev, Jaidev, Ravidas
tomorrow: what does courage feel like in your hands?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the true warrior: Kabir's fighter who stands for the deen and never leaves the field. Today, the last voices of Maru, and an argument about what one of them meant.
screen: `THE TRUE WARRIOR.` → `NOW, THE LAST VOICES OF MARU.`

segments.voice: Gym class, picking teams. The kid who always gets chosen last is suddenly named captain, and the whole room goes quiet. Who did that? Ravidas asks a question like that on ang 1106, about himself. He was born into a family people of his time refused to touch, and he writes: who but You would put a royal canopy over my head? So here's today's argument. Is that canopy about how people treat each other, or about the soul?
screen: `PICKED LAST. NAMED CAPTAIN.` → `A CANOPY OVER MY HEAD.` → `SOCIETY, OR THE SOUL?`

segments.voice: These final pages of Maru hold short hymns by three Bhagats: Namdev, Jaidev and Ravidas. Ravidas's hymn, in paraphrase: O Beloved, who but You could do such a thing? Cherisher of the poor, You set a royal canopy over my head. The one whose touch the world thought polluting, on him You poured mercy. My Lord raises the low up high, and fears no one. Then he names others who crossed over, Namdev, Kabir, Trilochan, Sadhna, Sain. Now, two readings, both held by thoughtful Sikhs. The first says: this is about the world. Ravidas names his own shunned birth, out loud, in scripture. The Gurus then put his words in the Granth, and built a community where everyone eats seated together in langar. The canopy is dignity, here, among real people. The second says: this is about the soul. The canopy isn't social rank; it's honor before God, and before God, worldly rank never mattered in either direction. Push on rank too hard and you've made it important again. Each side has a strong case. The first keeps the hymn from floating away into the clouds. The second keeps it from shrinking into only a social program. Either way, the hymn's question stands. Who but You.
screen: `NAMDEV, JAIDEV, RAVIDAS.` · `A CANOPY OVER MY HEAD.` · `READING ONE: DIGNITY HERE.` · `READING TWO: HONOR BEFORE GOD.` · then, large: `WHO BUT YOU.`

segments.voice: Let your head bow forward a little, chin toward your chest, the way you might feel when you've been overlooked. Then, slowly, over a few breaths, lift it until you're looking straight ahead, as if something were being held over you. Stay there, level, for the rest of the sit.

howItsDone: The Maru hymns of Namdev, Jaidev and Ravidas are sung in kirtan and read in order in a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib; Ravidas's 'aisee laal tujh bin kaun karai' is a well-known kirtan hymn.
